nodes.label: Get a California birth certificate
nodes.description: Identify the correct vital records office, choose an authorized or informational copy, and submit the required identity statement.

nodes.label: Choose the copy type
nodes.description: Authorized copies can be used to establish identity; informational copies cannot. Eligibility rules apply to authorized copies.

nodes.label: Choose the correct office
nodes.description: California Department of Public Health and county recorder offices handle copies. The best route can depend on the event date and county.

nodes.label: Submit the application and identity statement
nodes.description: Use the current state or county form and follow notarization and payment instructions for your chosen submission method.

nodes.label: Start and register a business in California
nodes.description: Choose a business structure, register where required, handle tax accounts, and check local permits.

nodes.label: Check licenses and local permits
nodes.description: Use CalGold and your city or county to identify permits and registrations for your location and activity.

nodes.label: Choose a structure and name
nodes.description: Compare legal and tax implications before filing. Check name availability and any naming rules for the structure you choose.

nodes.label: Register the entity if required
nodes.description: Corporations, LLCs, and limited partnerships generally file with the Secretary of State. Other structures may use county filings.

nodes.label: Set up tax accounts
nodes.description: Check whether you need a federal EIN and register for applicable California tax programs.

nodes.label: Get or replace a California driver’s license
nodes.description: Use the California DMV route for a first license, renewal, or replacement and bring the documents listed for that transaction.

nodes.label: Finish online or at a DMV office
nodes.description: Some transactions can be completed online. Others require an appointment, documents, photo, test, or in-person identity verification.

nodes.label: Complete the application and document check
nodes.description: Use the DMV checklist for the exact transaction before visiting an office or paying online.

nodes.label: Choose your transaction
nodes.description: The DMV uses different routes for a first license, renewal, replacement, name change, and REAL ID upgrade.

nodes.label: Get a California REAL ID
nodes.description: Apply through the California DMV, upload or gather the required documents, and complete identity verification in person.

nodes.label: Decide whether you need a REAL ID
nodes.description: A passport or another federally accepted document may meet your federal identification need. Check the official guidance before applying.

nodes.label: Gather the required documents
nodes.description: Use the DMV checklist for proof of identity, Social Security number, and California residency. Requirements depend on your documents and name history.

nodes.label: Complete the DMV visit
nodes.description: Start the application online when available, then bring the required originals to a DMV office for verification.

nodes.label: Apply for California unemployment benefits
nodes.description: Review eligibility, create or use myEDD, file a claim, and keep certifying for benefits while the claim is active.

nodes.label: Certify for benefits
nodes.description: Continue certifying for each period requested and report work or earnings accurately while the claim is active.

nodes.label: File the claim
nodes.description: Use UI Online through myEDD or another method listed by EDD. Save confirmations and respond to follow-up requests.

nodes.label: Review basic eligibility
nodes.description: EDD evaluates work history, earnings, availability for work, and the reason you are no longer working.

nodes.label: Gather employment information
nodes.description: Prepare identity, contact, and recent employer information using EDD's current checklist.

nodes.label: Register to vote in California
nodes.description: Check eligibility, register or update your record, and confirm your status through the Secretary of State.

nodes.label: Check your voter status
nodes.description: Use the state voter status tool or contact your county elections office to confirm your record and election information.

nodes.label: Check eligibility
nodes.description: Review California’s citizenship, residency, age, and status requirements before submitting a registration.

nodes.label: Register or update your record
nodes.description: Use the official online registration system or another state-approved method. Re-register after relevant name, address, or party changes.

nodes.label: Apply for CalFresh food benefits
nodes.description: Submit a CalFresh application, complete the county interview, and provide requested verification.

nodes.label: Submit an application
nodes.description: Apply online through BenefitsCal or use a method offered by your county. You can begin with basic contact information and complete the rest as directed.

nodes.label: Complete the county interview
nodes.description: Your county will contact you for an interview and explain what verification is needed for your household.

nodes.label: Provide requested verification
nodes.description: Submit only the documents your county requests, watch for notices, and use the appeal information on a notice if you disagree with a decision.

nodes.label: Apply for federal disaster assistance
nodes.description: Confirm that your area and loss qualify for an open disaster program, document damage, and apply through DisasterAssistance.gov.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Apply and save the registration number
nodes.description: Apply through DisasterAssistance.gov or another FEMA-approved channel, then respond to inspection or document requests.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Check the declared disaster and available help
nodes.description: Use DisasterAssistance.gov to see whether assistance is available for your location and situation.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Document damage and contact insurance
nodes.description: Photograph damage when safe, keep receipts, and notify your insurer. FEMA may ask about insurance coverage and decisions.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Address immediate safety needs
nodes.description: Follow local emergency instructions first. Government assistance applications do not replace emergency response or insurance notification.

audience: People affected by a federally declared disaster

nodes.label: Get an Employer Identification Number
nodes.description: Confirm that your organization needs an EIN, form the entity first when applicable, and apply directly with the IRS.

nodes.label: Apply directly with the IRS
nodes.description: Use an official IRS application method. The IRS does not charge for an EIN.

nodes.label: Form the legal entity first
nodes.description: If you are creating an LLC, corporation, partnership, or exempt organization, complete the state formation step before requesting the EIN.

nodes.label: Confirm that you need an EIN
nodes.description: The IRS explains when a business or organization needs an EIN and when a responsible party may apply.

nodes.label: Apply for federal student aid with the FAFSA form
nodes.description: Create the required StudentAid.gov accounts, gather financial information, submit the FAFSA form, and review school requests.

audience: Contributors to a student’s FAFSA form

nodes.label: Lake Vermilion-Soudan Underground Mine State Park
nodes.description: The Soudan Underground Mine was Minnesota’s first iron ore mine – the Soudan Mine – opened in 1882. The operations went underground by 1892 after numerous accidents. The mine’s value was in the special kind of ore it produced. The ore’s high oxygen content was used to make high-quality steel in open-hearth furnaces. When technology changed, the ore from the mine was no longer needed. Low-cost ores of the Mesabi Range took over. Soudan Mine stopped mining ore in 1962. Today you can explore the last level that the miners worked. More information about the Soudan Underground Mine can be found by visiting www.mndnr.gov/vermilionsoudan

All dogs are required to be licensed annually.

All dog licenses are renewed in January of each year. Any application received on, or after February 1st of each year will be considered late. Applications where an owner has acquired a new dog or has moved into the city within the previous 30 days shall not be considered late.
All dogs over the age of three months are required to be licensed. Newly acquired dogs must be licensed within 30 days.
Dog owners must be 18 years or older and possess proof of current rabies vaccination for the animal.

The cost of a dog license is $30, however a license for a dog that has been spayed/neutered is only $15. Any dog license that is determined to be “late” shall incur a late fee equal to the normal license fee.
A license may be purchased by clicking on the dog license application link below.
To be in possession of an unlicensed dog, even if that animal does not leave your property, is unlawful and may result in citation. Your dog must be wearing its license at all times.
dog licenses are now done online. please apply below
For residents with more than 4 dogs, a kennel license is required.
All kennel licenses are renewed in January of each year. Any application received on, or after February 1st of each year will be considered late.
A small kennel license (harboring five (5) to nine (9) dogs) shall be one hundred dollars ($100.00).

A large kennel license (harboring ten (10) or more dogs but not to exceed forty (40) dogs) shall be one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00). For each dog over the forty (40) dog limit, the cost shall increase by ten dollars ($10.00) for each dog.
Any dog license that is determined to be “late” shall incur a late fee equal to the normal license fee.
Before the license can be issued the following conditions of the kennel must be met:

The location where the dogs are kept, raised, housed, or boarded must be two hundred (200) feet away from any neighboring house, and; Must be one hundred fifty (150) feet from any road. The following minimum standards shall be complied with to obtain and maintain a kennel permit: Enclosure must be provided which shall allow adequate protection against weather extremes. Floors of buildings, runs and walls shall be of an appropriate material as required by the specific breed of animal and also to permit proper cleaning and disinfecting. Adequate ventilation shall be maintained and an appropriate temperature provided as required by the specific breed of animal housed therein. Each animal shall have sufficient space to stand up, lie down and turn around without touching the sides or tops of cages. Runs shall provide an adequate exercise area and protection from the weather. All animal quarters and runs are to be kept clean, dry and in a sanitary condition. The food shall be free of contamination, palatable and of sufficient nutritive value as to meet the normal daily requirements for the condition and size of the animal. Fresh water is to be available at all times. Water vessels shall be mounted or secured in a manner that prevents tipping and be of the removable type.

Holders of existing kennel permits which do not meet the distance requirements required in this section shall be exempt from the distance requirements for their existing animals. As animals die, are sold, given away, or are otherwise removed from the property, they may not be replaced unless all of the conditions of this section are met. The city shall have the power to revoke the kennel permit in the event that the permit holder is convicted of any other violation of the provisions of this title.
A kennel license may be purchased by clicking on the kennel license application link below.

tags: View the Village's Water Service Line Inventory Here!

In 2022, the Village of Carpentersville began assessing water service lines in Old Town, where there are known installations of lead water service lines. The Phase A construction to replace known lead water service lines began in the Fall of 2023 with additional phases to follow in the near future. However, with the determination and support from residents, the Village completed the replacement of all known water lead service lines in December of 2024 and entered 2025 as a lead-free water service line community!

The Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (IEPA) requires that all community's with water supply submit a water service line material inventory and a lead water service line replacement plan. On April 15, 2024, the Village of Carpentersville submitted the inventory and replacement plan which can be found at the links above. An updated inventory with displaying no known water lead service lines was submitted on March 14, 2025 and can also be viewed at the links above.

If you have any questions about the Village's Lead Water Service Line Replacement Program, please contact the Public Works Department Management Analyst, Nikki Ang, at 224-293-1626. Comments and feedback regarding the Lead Water Service Line Replacement Plan are also to be directed to the Public Works Department at 224-293-1626 or via email at nang@cville.org.

nodes.description: Stormwater is the discharge of water due to runoff from precipitation. Stormwater runoff occurs when precipitation from rain or snow melt flows over impervious surfaces. Impervious surfaces are areas that impede the infiltration of water into the soil. Concrete, asphalt, rooftops and even severely compacted areas of soil are considered impervious. Stormwater can pick up debris, chemicals, dirt, and other pollutants. These substances are then carried into storm sewer systems or to a waterway.

nodes.label: Well Permit / Abandonment Program
nodes.description: Any private well on a property in the City must be permitted or abandoned per City of Burlington Ordinance Number 1540(15). The well abandonment/permit program gives a private well owner the option to either continue using the well, if it is permitted, or to properly abandon the well. Unused and improperly abandoned wells are a significant threat to contamination of groundwater quality, and the Burlington Water Utility is responsible to insure that safe water will be supplied to its customers. This ordinance will allow for continued use of private wells if proper steps are taken. It also outlines the steps that must be taken to properly abandon a well.

tags: ** WE HAVE A NEW ALERT PROGRAM **
As of July 1, 2026 we will no longer use Everbridge for our community alerting & notification network. We will be transitioning to Motorola Rave and Smart911.

If you had enrolled with the previous Everbridge notification system, you MUST re-enroll with the new Rave/Smart911 system to receive alerts & notifications. Your Everbridge account will NOT transfer over to the new Rave/Smart911 system.
RESIDENT ALERT SYSTEM INFORMATION FOR THE CITY OF BRAIDWOOD

By enrolling in the Braidwood Community Alert Network, you can now stay connected by receiving up to the minute Emergency Alerts from local officials regarding immediate or pending threats to public safety or property, where immediate notification is necessary. Examples include evacuation recommendations, boil orders, water main breaks, and crime alerts.

You can also elect to receive Announcements, Notices, and Public Safety Non-Emergency information sent to your home phone, work phone, texted to your cell phone, or emailed to you. You can select how you receive the information based on the contact information you provide during the sign up process. Examples include:

- Announcements & Notices - May inform you of scheduled water and sewer repairs, changes in garbage pick-up and community press releases. Messages may also inform you of scheduled street closures, resurfacing projects, parking bans and local festivals.

- Public Safety Non-Emergency Information - May include messages from local officials with information about crime prevention information, public safety events, neighborhood crime alert information, and fire hydrant testing.

We have launched a new Mass Notification service that allows us to alert you. You opt-in to enter your contact information and subscribe to notification you care about based on your location. The information you provide is protected and will not be used for any other purpose.

When we issue a notification about a potential safety hazard or concern, you will receive a message on the voice or text communication methods that you have registered. If requested for the notification, you can confirm that you have received the message and you will not be contacted by any subsequent methods regarding that particular notification. If you do not confirm, the system will continue to attempt to reach you at all of the contact paths that you have registered.

Create a Smart911 account and add your contact and location information into the Mass Notification system. All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential. You can include as much or as little information that you wish. If you do not have access to a computer or Smartphone, or need help with registering, in-person assistance request forms can be obtained at Braidwood City Hall.
You can stop receiving at any time by removing your contact information from your profile.
